verdict: Amazon's sales rose 11% to $158.9B and operating income jumped 56% to $17.4B as AWS grew 19% and earned $10.4B — and it kept $15.3B as profit.

segments.name: North America
segments.note: Stores, subscriptions and ads in North America — the biggest piece, and it earned a $5.7B operating profit.

segments.name: International
segments.note: The same businesses outside North America — swung to a $1.3B operating profit after a small loss a year earlier.

segments.name: AWS
segments.note: Cloud computing rented to other companies — grew 19%, and its $10.4B operating profit was 60% of Amazon's total.

opex.name: Fulfillment
opex.note: Running the warehouses and delivering packages — the biggest single running cost.

opex.name: Technology & infrastructure
opex.note: Servers, data centers, and the engineers who build and run the products.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Advertising Amazon's products and winning customers.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Back office — finance, legal and management.

opex.name: Other operating expense, net
opex.note: Small net charges that do not fit the other lines.

otherDetail: Interest income $1,256M, less $603M interest expense and $27M of other expense, net; a $3M equity-method investment loss is recorded below the tax line.
follow100Note: AWS alone earned $10.4B of operating profit — 60% of Amazon's total — on just $17.28 of every $100 of sales. The rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: AWS kept accelerating
takeaways.text: AWS sales grew 19% to $27.5B and the segment earned $10.4B of operating profit — 60% of Amazon's total — as companies moved more computing, and new AI work, onto its cloud.

takeaways.title: Operating income jumped 56%
takeaways.text: Consolidated operating income rose 56% from a year ago: North America earned $5.7B and International swung from a small loss to a $1.3B profit as the store networks got more efficient.

takeaways.title: Stores grew steadily into the holidays
takeaways.text: Store sales grew 9% in North America and 12% internationally, helped by record-fast delivery speeds and a record Prime Big Deal Days event in October.
